chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Taking over the Strand Ballroom as Price's Palace
summary: After Reese Dupree's money dealings, Price buys the Strand Ballroom with Ike Levy's help and renames it Price's Palace, but gives up.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So I had a pretty good stint in Philadelphia. While I was there the Strand Ballroom was owned by Reese Dupree. I don't know if you know who that was.
But Reese Dupree owned the Strand Ballroom. We had a concert, Reese and I. We had Ella and Cootie Williams' band. And after the concert, Reese had a bunch of guys with him.

They took all the money and put it in a bag and Reese sat down and put that bag on his chair, and these guys were standing around him. So I said, "Well Reese, let's check up." He said, "Price, I just can't help it." I said, "Can't help what?" He start telling me what he owe and how many; I said, "Okay."

I went to Ike Levy and I asked Ike to get me Abbott Greenfield who owned the Strand Ballroom. And I entered into a tentative agreement to buy the building where the Strand Ballroom was operating. I got possession of the building and I evicted Reese Dupree and I changed the name of the Strand Ballroom to Price's Palace. And that's a matter of history, you know, and can be corroborated.

Well, I knew I couldn't hold on to it...keep it, because how could you have a dance hall, have a building, and have a dance hall, that's dark six days and then an occasional dance and then, you know, maybe you'll make it and maybe you won't. So that was...finally I gave up and in '48 I went to Europe instead of Willie "the Lion" Smith, and then I just took a different course. My life took a different course.
